question: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is an ophthalmic emergency because the inner retina can tolerate ischaemia for only approximately 90 minutes before irreversible damage occurs.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The 90-minute threshold for irreversible retinal damage makes CRAO a true ophthalmic emergency comparable to acute ischaemic stroke. Immediate management — ocular massage, carbogen inhalation, IOP lowering — aims to restore perfusion urgently.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Like cerebral ischaemia, CRAO has a tight time window. Irreversible retinal damage begins within 90–100 minutes of complete arterial occlusion. Urgent measures (ocular massage, IOP-lowering, consideration of thrombolysis) must be initiated immediately.
